methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $10M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 5 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $1.1B - $2.0B.

private.name: Humanoid
private.rationale: Same sector (Robotics & Manufacturing), same stage (Series A), post-money $1.35B

data.narrative:
Aestus Industries is a Series A robotics and manufacturing company founded by Ryan Hannifin, having raised $10M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparables universe of nine private robotics firms and one public company, with five peers constituting the primary peer set: Generalist AI, Bedrock Robotics, Dexterity, Humanoid, and Walden Robotics, spanning Seed through Series B stages.

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-Progression, anchoring to the $10M raised as a proxy for current value and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A progression, yields $20M. Peer-Median triangulation across the five same-sector comparables produces a median valuation of $1.6B, with a range spanning $1.1B (Walden Robotics, Seed) to $2.0B (Generalist AI, Series B).

The analytical range is $17M to $1.9B, with a midpoint of $835M. This wide dispersion reflects material stage and maturity differences within the peer set; the Stage-Progression method substantially underweights Aestus relative to later-stage comparable valuations. Key uncertainties include whether peer valuations reflect recent market repricing, the degree to which Aestus's technology or market position justifies premium or discount positioning within the peer range, and the relevance of Series B peers to a Series A company's current fair value.
